load fails loudly when counts differ after ILP send
docker/questdb compose publishes the ILP port or docs state the manual run requirement
context: Related done item perf-questdb-influxdb-load-20261030. Pre-existing: reproduced on the commit before #3952. Not fixed by the verifier.
description:
Found by live verification of #3952 (perf-questdb-influxdb-load-20261030) on origin/develop 525361b2f8 against questdb/questdb:10.0.1 (started with `mocker run` publishing 9009 because docker/questdb/docker-compose.yml publishes only 19000, 8812 and 9003, so the ILP path cannot be used against the repo's stack as shipped).

Reproduction: generate TPC-H SF0.01 with `--compression none`, then `benchbox run --platform questdb --benchmark tpch --scale 0.01 --phases load --compression none --platform-option loading_method=ilp --platform-option http_port=19000 --platform-option ilp_port=9009 --platform-option pg_port=8812`. Then count rows per table.
Expected: every table has the dbgen row count (orders 15000, partsupp 8000, supplier 100).
Actual: orders 10947, partsupp 6505, supplier below 100 on the SF0.01 chunked data (baseline commit 7aa4a8b391, before #3952, also loses rows: orders 13589, partsupp 6272, supplier 90), with the load reporting SUCCESS. Logs /tmp/live-verify-questdb-check.log and /tmp/live-verify-questdb-check-base3952.log.
Isolation: sending the same Arrow-built lines for partsupp over ONE socket gives 8000/8000; opening a new socket per chunk file and closing it immediately gives 6759 and 6979 of 8000 (/tmp/lv/ilp_probe.py). So the loss is the per-file connect/send/close pattern in QuestDBAdapter._load_table_via_ilp (benchbox/platforms/questdb.py): ILP-over-TCP gives no acknowledgement and the adapter never waits for the server to apply data before closing. #3952's line builder itself is correct: orders over one socket loads 15000/15000, 14999 order dates identical to the file, one injected unparseable o_orderdate row keeps all other columns and gets server time (/tmp/live-verify-questdb-ilp-orders.log).

Suspected: _load_table_via_ilp and the per-file loop in load_data; fix by one connection per table or by confirming row counts after sending (and failing the load on mismatch).
